articles.title: Dolly Parton Has Died, and Her Family’s Announcement Is Completely “Dolly” in Its Comfort and Inspiration
articles.content:
### 传奇巨星多莉·帕顿过世，享年80岁

多莉·帕顿——来自田纳西州大烟山的金发乡村歌手，这位光芒四射的明星于2月底去世，享年80岁。从1966年发行首支单曲开始，她便以灿烂的笑容和感人的歌声照亮了无数人的生活，将被我们永远怀念。

我初次接触多莉是在1980年经典电影《9到5》中，这部开创性影片不仅展示了她奇特的音乐才华——她用指甲“打”出了“型打字机”的音效——还展现了她出色的喜剧表演和演技。至今，我和兄弟仍常引用电影中的台词调侃对方。甚至连我的黄金犬，我都以她的名字命名，每次去兽医诊所或狗公园都会引来笑声。

多莉·帕顿以其传染性的人格魅力和非凡才能，在每个人心中留下了难忘的印记。当我们仍在消化这令人震惊的消息时——尽管去年她的健康状况已经让人忧心——让我们一起为她的家人默哀，而她的家人以多莉一贯的风格宣布了她的去世，这正是她希望的方式。她定会欣喜地知道我们都在怀念她。

### 多莉的家人透露其去世消息并致敬其遗产
多莉的侄子兼保镖布莱恩·西弗（Bryan Seaver）在Instagram上分享了这一令人心碎的消息，并谈到多莉留下的永恒遗产。

“能够以这样的方式分享消息，我们感到既骄傲又悲伤。”西弗说，“悲伤属于我们，而多莉已在光明中，在耶稣的怀抱中，迎接她的还有卡尔、她的父母以及无数在天堂等待她的人。”卡尔·托马斯·迪恩（Carl Thomas Dean）是多莉长期以来的丈夫，两人于1966年结婚，迪恩去年去世，享年82岁。

西弗回忆了自己孩童时代在1980年代初次体验“巡演生活”，并感谢多莉为他的家庭以及无数歌手、词曲作者、音乐人和各行各业的追梦者开辟了道路。“她从未见到过她打不开的门，而那些她打开的门改变了历史。”

他还承认我们都深受打击，并加入了一丝多莉特有的幽默：“我的家庭和多莉共享了一生的美好回忆，但你们也一样。她一直在你们的电视、唱片机、CD和手机播放列表中，成为你们家庭的一部分，无论你们是否愿意。”这句话既体贴又有趣，让粉丝们感受到了她的关怀。

### 多莉的健康问题和最终的离世
自从去年丈夫去世后，多莉对健康问题变得更加坦率。她先是推迟了去年在拉斯维加斯的个人演唱会，后来取消了。她在社交媒体上发帖安抚忧心的粉丝：“我还没死呢。”

今年5月，她分享了自己对免疫和消化系统问题的治疗取得积极进展的消息，称这些问题“搞砸了”。多莉在这些信息中透露了她积极的性格，但显然情况比我们想象的更严重。

多莉的经纪人透露，她因癌症去世。多莉于上周五入院于纳什维尔范德比尔特-英格拉姆癌症中心，在亲人的陪伴下离世。

### 多莉的辉煌成就与慈善事业
多莉·帕顿是一位精明的商人，她清楚地知道自己需要克服多少障碍才能在音乐行业立足。她首支单曲《傻瓜金发女郎》（"Dumb Blonde"）的名字讽刺地暗示了她的才智，而这正是她成为传奇人物的最初征兆。

在长达六十年的职业生涯中，多莉创作了超过3000首歌曲，并将自己定位为“故事歌手”而非歌手、演员、主题公园老板、儿童慈善家和国家瑰宝。从杰克·怀特（Jack White）到瑞巴·麦金泰尔（Reba McEntire），许多音乐人都翻唱过她的歌曲，纷纷致敬。

在COVID-19大流行期间，她捐赠了100万美元用于研究，最终促成了莫德纳疫苗的问世。2016年，她捐赠了900万美元帮助田纳西州的山火受害者。她也致力于提升儿童识字率。1995年，她成立了“想象图书馆”，以纪念她从未学会读写的父亲罗伯特·李·帕顿（Robert Lee Parton）。该组织向全球儿童捐赠了数亿本书。

多莉的成就太多，以至于很难一一列举。除了格莱美奖、乡村音乐奖和慈善奖项，我认为她最持久的遗产将是她给人们带来的感受。没有人能像多莉一样。她超凡的个性和慷慨的精神感染着每一个人，即使她开玩笑自嘲自己的外表或令人共鸣的小缺点，也能让我们跟着她开怀大笑。

### 多莉的离世引发了全球的哀悼
当人们在社交媒体上分享多莉去世的消息时，各行各业的人们都纷纷表达了对她的敬意。从音乐人到普通粉丝，所有人都在怀念这位传奇人物，她的离世在全球范围内引发了广泛的哀悼。

多莉·帕顿的一生充满了传奇色彩，她的音乐和慈善事业将继续影响世界。她的离世让我们失去了一位伟大的艺术家和慈善家，但她的精神和作品将永远被世人铭记。
articles.summary:
It’s the news no one wanted to hear but we were all bracing for: Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80. The brash blond songwriter from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee has been a bright light in our lives ever since she released her first song back in 1966, and we will miss her.

I fell in love with Dolly in 9 to 5, the groundbreaking 1980 movie that not only showcased her innovative musical talent (she played the “typewriter” on her fingernails) but also her comedy and acting chops. My brother and I still quote the movie to each other as a running gag, and I named my barrel-chested blond dog Dolly Parton, which never fails to get a laugh at the vet or dog park.

No doubt you also have many memories of Dolly Parton and her infectious personality and incredible talents. While we process this devastating news, which somehow comes as a huge shock even as we worried over the last year or so about her health, let’s take a moment to grieve with her family, who announced her death in a way we think Dolly would approve. She would likely be tickled to know that we’re all remembering her too.

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more celebrity news, humor, travel, tech and fun facts all week long.

What did her family say in their announcement of her passing?

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Dolly Parton (@dollyparton)


In an Instagram post, Bryan Seaver, Parton’s nephew and head of security (like his father before him), shared the news of her death and spoke of Dolly’s lasting legacy.

“It is an honor, but an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly,” Seaver said. “Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed to meet her in the heavens.” Carl Thomas Dean was Parton’s longtime but reclusive husband, whom she married in 1966. Dean died last year at the age of 82.

Seaver shared how he first got a taste of the “road life” as a kid in the 1980s, and he thanked his Aunt Dolly for opening doors for his family and generations of singers, songwriters, musicians and dreamers from every walk of life. “She never saw a door she couldn’t open, and the doors she did open made and changed history.”

He also acknowledged how much we were hurting and added a little characteristic Dolly humor: “My family and I have shared a lifetime of beautiful memories with Dolly, but so have you. She has always been on your television, your record player, your CD and on your phone playlist, becoming an extended part of your family, whether you liked it or not.” It was a sweet, funny nod that made fans feel seen.

Had Dolly been ill recently?

Yes. Since her husband died last year, Dolly had been open, if characteristically tongue-in-cheek, about her health struggles. After postponing and then canceling a Las Vegas residency last year, she posted an update on social media to assure her millions of adoring, worried fans: “I ain’t dead yet.”

Then, in May of this year, she shared news that she responded positively to treatments for immune and digestive issues that had “got all out of whack.” Dolly’s sunny personality shone through in these cryptic messages, but clearly things were darker than we’d all hoped.

The cause of death was cancer, her spokesperson said. Dolly was admitted to the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville on Friday, and she died surrounded by loved ones, according to the New York Times.

What will Dolly’s legacy be?

A shrewd businesswoman, Dolly knew she had to overcome hurdles to be taken seriously in the music business, and her first song, ironically titled “Dumb Blonde” (she was anything but), gave us all a hint of the clever powerhouse she would become.

Dolly penned more than 3,000 songs in her six-decade career and always considered herself a “songteller” rather than a singer, actor, theme park owner, kids charity benefactor and all-around national treasure that she came to be. Tributes from musicians who have covered her songs over the years—from Jack White to Reba McEntire—are pouring in.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, she donated $1 million to research that eventually produced Moderna’s vaccine, and in 2016, she gave $9 million to victims of wildfires in her home state of Tennessee. She also was dedicated to childhood literacy. In 1995, she started the Imagination Library in honor of her father, Robert Lee Parton, who never learned to read or write. The organization has donated hundreds of millions of books to kids around the world.

Dolly had so many accomplishments that it’s honestly hard to list them all. Beyond her Grammys, Country Music Awards and humanitarian accolades, I imagine her lasting legacy will be how she made people feel. There’s no one like Dolly. Her larger-than-life personality and generous spirit were infectious, and even when she was poking fun at her appearance and totally relatable foibles, she made us laugh right along with her.
